node.title: PROVED/VERIFIED (X-10): the low-q split-pair falsifier — p >= n^2 is nearly sharp
node.statement: At h = 2, split pairs are sum collisions (L_{a,b} determined by a+b, ab); charged pairs are EXACTLY the antipodal-sum ones (the fiber-product line X+Y = s is toral iff s = 0); pigeonhole gives uncharged > n^2 whenever q < ~n^2/7. VERIFIED EXACT INSTANCE: n = 64, p = 193: 18,816 uncharged vs n^2 = 4,096 (charged = 992 = 32*31 exactly, matching the antipodal count). The trigger decreases in h (h = 2 is worst), so p >= n^2 kills the mechanism at every h; official rows sit 48.8 bits above the h = 2 trigger. The X-8 pigeonhole lesson, miniaturized and now built into the theorem's hypotheses as a nearly-sharp condition.
node.notes: X-10 phase 1. Also verified: sparse-relation seeds do not amplify to uncharged split pairs above the threshold (pullback amplification is cyclically charged).
